metadata.remarks:
Identity Lifecycle defines the capability to establish, modify, suspend, revoke, and terminate identities throughout their institutional existence. This includes lifecycle events for both human and non-human identities and ensures access remains aligned with current status.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for roles and responsibilities, SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance activities related to identity lifecycle management. Controls are intentionally scoped to individual lifecycle stages.

components.title: Onboarding
components.description: Controlled creation and initial activation of identities, including assignment of attributes and baseline entitlements.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Establish organizational user identities as part of onboarding.
Create accounts in accordance with defined account management procedures.

components.title: Changes in Status
components.description: Updates to identity attributes and entitlements resulting from role, affiliation, or status changes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Modify accounts and privileges when user status changes.
Maintain least privilege following changes in identity status.

components.title: Suspension and Revocation
components.description: Temporary or permanent disabling of identities in response to policy, risk, or separation events.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Restrict access dynamically based on identity status.

components.title: Deprovisioning
components.description: Permanent removal of identities and associated access following end of affiliation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Remove or permanently disable accounts when no longer required.
Terminate identity records in accordance with lifecycle policies.
